description: Pediatric case — parent reporting a brief febrile seizure in a 3-year-old. Child has now stopped seizing but is drowsy. Multiple known conditions and parental panic.

mock_input.raw_transcript: My son is 3 years old and he just had a seizure — his whole body was shaking for maybe a minute or two. He has a fever, it started yesterday. He’s not shaking anymore but he’s very sleepy and kind of not responding properly, just staring. He’s had a febrile seizure once before when he was two. He also has asthma. I’m terrified, what do I do?

ideal_output.priority_rationale: A generalised seizure in a 3-year-old with ongoing fever and post-ictal altered consciousness requires immediate emergency evaluation. The brief duration and self-resolution are reassuring but are insufficient to downgrade priority — serious neurological and infectious causes cannot be excluded, particularly given the child’s reduced responsiveness and high fever. A known history of prior seizure activity does not lower urgency in this presentation. Comorbid respiratory conditions warrant additional monitoring. Immediate paediatric emergency assessment is indicated.
